name: @oscharko-dev/keiko-ui
description: Keiko Wave 1 local UI (static export). Build-time-only; served by the Node BFF in keiko-server.

scripts.typecheck:native: npm --prefix ../.. run check:typescript-toolchain && node ../../node_modules/@typescript/native/bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit --incremental false

_browserslistRationale: Corrected from chrome/edge>=79, firefox>=72, safari>=13.1, which the shipped UI code has not
satisfied for a long time: Array.prototype.at(-n) appears 35 times across 22 production files
(Firefox 90, Safari 15.4), crypto.randomUUID 19 times across 13 (Firefox 95, Safari 15.4),
Object.hasOwn 7 times across 6 (Firefox 92), and lib/api.ts uses AbortSignal.timeout (Firefox
100, Safari 16) — every one beyond the old floor, so the declaration promised engines on which
the app cannot start. Counts are occurrences and files stated separately on purpose: the
gate's own messages report FILES, and conflating the two produced three wrong numbers here.
AbortSignal.any (Chrome 116, Firefox 124, Safari 17.4) sits above even these floors and is
feature-detected with a fallback in lib/api.ts rather than raising them further.
These floors correspond to the Baseline 'widely available' set and cover every JS API the UI calls.
Enterprise Windows fleets run evergreen Edge/Chrome, so this is not a reachability change for
them; it makes the declaration true. check:browser-baseline enforces it against the source.
Firefox is 121, not 111, because of CSS the gate now scans: 32 :has() rules across 6 stylesheets
DEFINE custom properties that later declarations consume (absent, not merely unstyled, below 121),
and globals.css uses oklch() 190x and color-mix() 590x (Firefox 113) with no @supports fallback —
an engine that cannot parse a colour value drops the whole declaration, which for a theme built on
them means unreadable text, not a cosmetic shift. Declarations that DO degrade gracefully
(text-wrap: balance) are deliberately not gated: listing them would manufacture pressure to raise
a support floor for a nicety.
Raised again (chrome/edge 111->126, firefox 121->126, safari 16.4->18) because
check:browser-baseline's DEPENDENCY_FILES scan (IDX58) found pdfjs-dist@6.2.108 — loaded by
PdfCitationPreviewWindow.tsx and shipped unmodified, no useBuiltIns polyfilling — unconditionally
calling Promise.withResolvers (Chrome 119, Firefox 121, Safari 17.4) on every getDocument() call
and URL.parse (Chrome 126, Firefox 126, Safari 18) on the URL-backed load path, plus the SAME
AbortSignal.any noted above, this time from code with no feature-detection to fall back on: a
dependency's own source cannot be patched to feature-detect the way lib/api.ts does. Switching
pdfjs-dist's legacy build entry does not avoid this — grepping node_modules/pdfjs-dist/legacy/
build/pdf.mjs finds the identical calls, since "legacy" only lowers Babel's SYNTAX target and
changes nothing about which runtime APIs the library calls. URL.parse is the binding constraint
